steps.title: Clean silicon wafers
steps.instruction: Submerge wafer in 50 mL acetone for 3 min, then 50 mL isopropyl alcohol for 2 min, then 100 mL deionized water for 2 min; rinse with a DI‑water spray bottle, dry with compressed nitrogen, and bake on a hotplate at 150 °C for at least 15 min. Allow to cool to room temperature before proceeding.

steps.title: Spin‑coat SU‑8 photoresist (general)
steps.instruction: Place wafer on spin‑coater centered, pour enough SU‑8 to cover ~50 mm diameter, spin: accelerate to 500 rpm at 100 rpm/s and hold 10 s, then accelerate to the required speed (see specific mold steps) at 300 rpm/s and hold 30 s, finally decelerate to 500 rpm at 100 rpm/s and hold 5 s.

steps.title: Soft bake (pre‑bake)
steps.instruction: Place wafer on a level hotplate at 65 °C for 1 min, ramp to 95 °C and hold for the time specified by the SU‑8 datasheet (depends on thickness), then reduce to 65 °C and remove.

steps.title: UV exposure
steps.instruction: Load wafer into mask aligner, align the photomask, and expose to UV; exposure time t = E/P where E is required energy (based on resist thickness) and P is lamp power.

steps.title: Post‑exposure bake
steps.instruction: Place wafer on hotplate at 65 °C for 1 min, ramp to 95 °C and hold for the time given by the SU‑8 datasheet, then slowly cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Develop photoresist
steps.instruction: Rinse wafer in propylene glycol methyl ether acetate (PGMEA) developer, agitate frequently for 5–10 min until features are clear; then rinse sequentially with isopropyl alcohol and DI water until runoff is clear, and dry gently with compressed air.

steps.title: Optional hard bake
steps.instruction: Place wafer on hotplate at 65 °C for 1 min, then 100 °C for 1 min, then 150 °C for 3 min (extend if cracks remain).

steps.title: Fabricate multi‑height dilution master
steps.instruction: Using cleaned wafer, spin‑coat SU‑8 3050 at 2000 rpm (target 90 µm), soft bake at 95 °C for 45 min, expose with first mask, post‑exposure bake at 95 °C for 5 min; spin‑coat SU‑8 2025 at 4200 rpm (target 37 µm), soft bake at 95 °C for 6 min, expose with second mask (herringbone ridges), post‑exposure bake at 95 °C for 12 min, develop as above, then hard bake as above.

steps.title: Fabricate single‑height cell injection master
steps.instruction: Clean wafer, spin‑coat SU‑8 3050 at 2550 rpm (target 75 µm), soft bake at 95 °C for 45 min, expose with cell‑injection mask, post‑exposure bake at 95 °C for 8 min, develop and hard bake as above.

steps.title: Silanize master molds
steps.instruction: Rinse each wafer with isopropyl alcohol then DI water, dry with nitrogen; place 1–2 drops of tridecafluoro‑1,1,2,2‑tetrahydrooctyl trichlorosilane onto a glass slide or weighing boat, put wafers and silane inside a vacuum desiccator for ≥1 h (filter silane to protect pump). Store wafers in fresh plastic Petri dishes with tape securing edges.

steps.title: Prepare PDMS mixture
steps.instruction: Mix SYLGARD™ 184 base and curing agent at 10:1 mass ratio (e.g., 30 g base + 3 g curing agent = 33 g total). Filter the mixture through a 0.2 µm syringe filter and store at 4 °C (use within 2 weeks).

steps.title: Cast PDMS on molds
steps.instruction: For each wafer, pour ~20–30 g PDMS (if re‑casting) or 80–100 g PDMS (first cast) to fully cover the wafer; degas in a vacuum desiccator for ≥10 min, pour over molds, return to desiccator for another ~10 min, optionally burst remaining bubbles with gentle compressed air, then cure in a level oven at 60–70 °C for ≥1 h until firm and non‑sticky.

steps.title: Demold and punch ports
steps.instruction: Cut PDMS slabs from the wafers with a precision knife, lift slabs carefully, tape both sides with Scotch tape for protection, and punch tubing ports (chemical inlet, buffer inlet, A_i, B_i for dilution layer; cell inlet and buffer inlet for injection layer) using a 1.5 mm biopsy punch, keeping punches perpendicular to the slab.

steps.title: Rinse and clean dilution PDMS
steps.instruction: Rinse the dilution‑layer PDMS with ethanol then DI water, blow‑dry with nitrogen, then clean surfaces by repeatedly applying and removing Scotch tape (leaving tape on features for dust protection).

steps.title: Clean glass slide
steps.instruction: Scrub a double‑wide glass slide (75 mm × 50 mm × 1 mm) with isopropyl‑alcohol‑soaked wipes, rinse with DI water, blow‑dry with nitrogen; optional harsher cleaning (H₂O₂ or HCl) may be used if needed.

steps.title: Bond dilution PDMS to glass
steps.instruction: Place the glass slide and the dilution‑layer PDMS (feature side up, tape removed) in a plasma oven, expose both surfaces for 60 s; immediately bring PDMS (now inverted) into contact with the glass, press gently to remove air gaps, then place on a hotplate at 110 °C for ≥30 min to covalently bond. Inspect under a microscope; if debris is present, flush with DI water or remake the slab.

steps.title: Bond cell‑injection PDMS to dilution layer
steps.instruction: Clean both PDMS surfaces (feature side of cell‑injection slab and exposed top of bonded dilution slab) with Scotch tape, leave tape for dust protection, plasma‑treat both surfaces for 60 s, invert the cell‑injection slab so channels face down, align its punched ports with those of the dilution layer by eye (or stereomicroscope), bring into contact, then hot‑plate at 110 °C for ≥1 h followed by 70 °C overnight. Store assembled device in a dust‑free container with tape covering the top.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 % w/v BSA solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.1 g BSA in 20 mL DI water, vortex thoroughly, filter through a 0.2 µm syringe filter, and store in a cool dark place until use.

steps.title: Degas assembled device (optional)
steps.instruction: Place the fully assembled MCD in a vacuum desiccator for 15 min (or up to 30 min if thickness is unknown) to remove trapped air from the device and PDMS.

steps.title: Prepare inlet syringes
steps.instruction: Take four 20 mL conical tubes, remove each plunger, attach a 23G Luer‑lock blunt needle, thread ~60 cm of Tygon tubing onto each needle, and mount the syringes (needle up) on a lab‑flask grip stand at ≥50 cm height.

steps.title: Fill syringes with BSA and connect
steps.instruction: Immediately after removing the device from the vacuum chamber, fill each syringe with the prepared 0.5 % BSA solution; as fluid exits the tubing, connect the tubing to the corresponding inlet of the MCD (chemical inlet, buffer inlet of dilution layer, cell inlet, buffer inlet of injection layer). Allow BSA flow to purge bubbles for 30–60 min (or overnight if no vacuum step).

steps.title: Prepare experimental inlet solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare four solutions: (1) chemo‑stimulus dissolved in appropriate buffer (concentration C₀) for the dilution‑layer chemical inlet; (2) buffer alone for the dilution‑layer buffer inlet; (3) washed cells resuspended in buffer for the cell‑injection inlet; (4) buffer alone for the cell‑injection buffer inlet. Use the same buffer (e.g., artificial seawater, M9 minimal medium) as appropriate for the organism.

steps.title: Attach experimental tubing
steps.instruction: Disconnect the BSA syringes, leaving a droplet on each inlet/outlet. Briefly turn on the pressure controller to form a small droplet at the end of each inlet tubing, then bring the tubing tip into contact with the droplet on the device, push in firmly (tug test), and repeat for all four inlets. Insert a 40 cm outlet tubing into the device outlet and connect to a waste container.

steps.title: Level fluid reservoirs
steps.instruction: Place the device on the microscope stage, ensure that the liquid‑air interfaces of all inlet containers and the outlet container are at the same height; adjust Falcon tube heights as needed to equalize hydrostatic pressure.

steps.title: Set up microscope acquisition
steps.instruction: Locate a mid‑plane observation point in each experimental channel, select a magnification that captures the full channel width (typically 4×–10×), and plan for ~10 min of image acquisition (longer for slow‑diffusing attractants).

steps.title: Calibrate flow pressure ratios
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL of 0.1 mM fluorescein in DI water and 100 mL DI water. Load the device as in the experimental setup, flowing fluorescein through both dilution‑layer inlets and DI water through the cell‑injection inlet, with fluorescein also in the cell‑injection buffer inlet. Set the pressure controller to the designed ratios (p_in,1‑2 = 100 mbar, p_in,3‑4 = 50 mbar). Observe three laminar streams (two fluorescent, one dark). Adjust p_in,3‑4 until the outer fluorescent widths (w₁ and w₃) are equal, then record the final pressure ratio. This calibrated ratio will be used for all devices made from the same molds.

steps.title: Run chemotaxis experiment
steps.instruction: After at least 2 min of continuous flow with the experimental solutions, stop the pressure controller, clamp the outlet tubing near its open end, and begin image acquisition. When acquisition is finished, unclamp the outlet, cut the crimped tubing, re‑fill syringes if needed, and repeat steps for additional technical replicates. Replace the cell suspension for new biological replicates.

steps.title: Prepare fluorescein stock solutions (reference)
steps.instruction: For 1 mM stock: dissolve 0.0941 g fluorescein sodium salt in 250 mL DI water. For 0.1 mM stock: mix 25 mL of the 1 mM stock with 225 mL DI water. Filter both stocks through 0.2 µm filters and store as described.
